prompt: Count the subsets of an n-element set: 2^n, computed with your own loop or recursion in a long (n up to 62) -- Math.pow is off limits because doubles lose precision at this size.
explanation: Each of the n elements independently chooses in-or-out, so the counts multiply: 2 * 2 * ... * 2, n times. Starting a long accumulator at 1 and doubling it n times computes 2^n exactly in integer arithmetic; n = 0 naturally returns 1 for the lone empty set. The n <= 62 limit exists because 2^63 overflows a signed long -- and Math.pow would silently round long before that, which is why it is banned here.
hints: Think per element: each one doubles the number of possible subsets.
long total = 1L; then a loop running n times doing total *= 2.
A one-line recursive version also works: n == 0 ? 1L : 2L * subsets(n - 1). Bit-shift fans can even write 1L << n.
